correctness.rationale: The source gives the graph-pushforward formula and proves \(g_1+g_2=-\varphi\), \(g_1g_2=-1\), \(\alpha_1+\alpha_2=1\), and \(\alpha_j=g_j^2/(1+g_j^2)\). These identities make the fiber weights probabilities. The support equation gives mean \(-\varphi\), second moment \(1+\varphi^2\), variance \(1\), and the complete moment recurrence. Direct partial fractions give the stated fiber Cauchy transform. The finite exceptional set is Lebesgue-null and does not alter the disintegration.

value.rationale: The source weights are introduced as residue factors for an extremality proof. The accepted result shows that they encode a canonical probability kernel with parameter-independent variance one and an exact moment recursion. It also identifies every real boundary slice as the Cauchy transform of that fiber law. This gives a reusable structural bridge between graph geometry, Nevanlinna representation, and finite-support moment methods rather than a cosmetic renaming of the source formulas.
